About

About Me

I am a Brazilian meteorologist and PhD candidate in the Department of Earth, Environmental, and Planetary Sciences at Brown University, working with Professor Amanda Lynch. My research examines Arctic weather systems, particularly polar lows, and their implications for maritime safety.

My work combines atmospheric dynamics, numerical weather prediction, and climate data analysis. Using Polar WRF simulations, sensitivity experiments, and observational datasets, I investigate the physical processes responsible for polar low development and intensification, including the roles of sea ice, ocean surface conditions, and atmospheric heating. I have also worked on machine learning applications to improve the spatial resolution of sea ice concentration data.

Before beginning my PhD, I worked as a meteorologist in Brazil, where I gained experience in operational weather forecasting and communicating severe weather risks. This experience continues to shape my interest in research that can contribute to better forecasts and more useful weather information.

Beyond the physical science, I am interested in the relationship between environmental change, maritime operations, and Arctic governance. My broader goal is to contribute to our understanding of hazardous weather in the Arctic while exploring how that knowledge can support safer decisions in a changing region.

Research

What I work on

My research combines atmospheric dynamics, numerical models, and environmental data to study weather and climate in high latitudes.

Atmospheric dynamics

Polar lows and Arctic storms

Using Polar WRF experiments to examine how sea ice, topography, surface fluxes, and storm processes affect the development and intensity of polar lows.

Storm development

Marine cold air outbreaks

Investigating how exposure to marine cold air outbreak conditions influences polar low development and why individual storms respond differently.

Machine learning

Sea ice and high resolution information

Applying generative adversarial networks to enhance sea ice concentration resolution in a strait along the Northern Sea Route.

Weather hazards

Arctic maritime safety

Examining severe weather hazards such as polar lows and ship icing, and their relevance for people operating in Arctic waters.

Forecast evaluation

Precipitation in Brazil

Evaluating subseasonal precipitation simulations in Brazil's São Francisco River Basin using the Eta model.

Research & practice

Forecast use and communication

Connecting modeling research with operational forecasting, public communication, and the practical interpretation of weather risks.
